evidence: profileControlService.requestDeletion pauses owned businesses and providers (owner_enabled = false) for the grace period, and cancelDeletion brings back exactly what was visible before. E2E critical/account-deletion asserts the storefront disappears for a guest and comes back after cancelling.

purge-deleted-accounts deleted businesses while bulk_deal_tokens.business_id references them with ON DELETE NO ACTION (production catalog 2026-09-16), and ignored the error — so the auth identity was deleted while the storefront stayed live. Claim passes are now deleted first and every step goes through mustDelete(), which throws. bulk_deal_campaigns never existed and that call is gone. Deployment of the edge function is an owner step.

profileControlService.exportBundle() adds bookings, queue visits, requests, proposals, agreements, messages sent, reviews written, community posts and comments, emergency contacts, payments, custom payments, reports filed and bug reports to the download (DataSettings 'Download my data'); reads go through RLS as the user.

/legal and /legal/:slug sit outside GuestOrAuthLayout and ProtectedLayout (src/App.tsx), so they stay reachable while deletion is pending; the deletion-pending screen links to the account-deletion policy.

Migration 20260981 adds profile_deletion_requests.prev_visibility; requestDeletion records customer_enabled and each owned business/provider's owner_enabled, and cancelDeletion restores exactly those (falling back to the old 'switch everything on' only for requests made before the column existed). Forced-rollback tested on staging (scratchpad/test_81.mjs).

The delete dialog now needs DELETE typed before the button enables (DataSettings), matching the admin console's typed confirmation. E2E critical/account-deletion asserts the button is disabled until then.

Migration 20260982: admin_delete_post, admin_delete_comment and admin_cancel_request write the author a notification quoting what was removed, before the row goes. Forced-rollback tested on staging: before 0 notices for 3 removals, after 3.

AdminPanel.takeAction acts on BUSINESS, PROVIDER, POST, REQUEST and COMMENT; anything else (RATING, USER, PROPOSAL) now stays OPEN with 'No automatic action for a reported <type> yet' instead of being filed as Action taken with the content still live. What those types should do is owner decision E2E-037.

20260978 audits report, business, provider, place, request, agreement and community-post moderation into public.admin_actions; 20260982 adds the missing comment removal (written inside admin_delete_comment, so deleting a post with many comments records one action, not one per reply). private.admin_action_logs (the table the claim names) is not reachable through PostgREST — see E2E-042.

Report cards show the reporter's note (E2E-030) plus 'Open the reported <type>' linking to the post, request, business, provider or user, so a moderator can read it before acting. Comments and ratings have no screen of their own and carry no link.

Confirmed: account_appeals covers BUSINESS and PROVIDER only, so someone whose post or comment was removed has no route back except support. With 20260982 the author is at least told what happened and pointed at support. A full content-appeal queue (entity types, admin screen, notifications) is a v1.1 feature — owner decision.

takeAction removes the content first and resolves the report second, so a failure leaves a retryable open report rather than a report marked resolved with the content still live; the RPCs are idempotent (delete by id), so the retry succeeds. E2E critical/admin-moderation drives the report → action → resolved path.

Every notifications realtime subscription carries filter user_id=eq.<uid> (Home, Profile, DesktopSidebar, ManageDashboard, ProviderDashboard, Notifications), so one user's notification doesn't wake every client.
DesktopSidebar's Bell badge reads its own notifUnread query (getUnreadCount scope CUSTOMER); chatUnread is on the Inbox row where it belongs.
NotificationSettings debounces the radius write by 400ms and skips it entirely when the value already matches the saved one.

With no ?scope=, badgeCacheKey now defaults to 'notif:customer' — the badge Home, Profile and the desktop sidebar read — so marking read updates it immediately instead of waiting for a realtime resync.

notificationService.list(scope, before) reads the page older than a timestamp and NOTIFICATION_PAGE_SIZE is shared with the screen, which shows 'Show older' once a full page is loaded and keeps older pages across realtime refetches.
A delete that fails puts the row back at the index it came from instead of appending it to the end, so it returns to its own day group.
'Mark all read' has minHeight 44 and horizontal padding, so it meets the 44px minimum touch target next to the back button.

The phone field in ProfileEdit is read-only and explains that the number is the login identity: editing it wrote public.users.phone with no OTP, desynced auth.users and published a number the account never proved it owns. Changing the login number needs an OTP flow (support-assisted for v1).
get_public_profile returns alias (production pg_get_function_result, 2026-09-16), so aliasName() uses the handle and doesn't fall back to the real first name.
Picking a photo uploads it and shows the preview, but the profile row is only written by Save changes — leaving the screen no longer changes the avatar permanently.
PublicProfile shows the neighbourhood when the member published it (showCityPublicly) or to themselves; only the exact distance still needs an accepted location request.
The hero rating badge renders only when isSelf || u.showRatingPublicly !== false (PublicProfile ~line 380).
ProfileEdit sends only the privacy switches flipped on that screen (touchedPrivacy ref), so saving can't write back a stale copy of a toggle changed meanwhile in Settings → Privacy.
An empty alias field now sends null and clears the handle; it used to drop out of the patch (cleanAlias || undefined), so an alias could be changed but never removed.
userService.update syncs lat/lng to the owner's provider profile alongside avatar and name, so a listing moves with its owner instead of staying at the old coordinates.
A hidden profile (customerEnabled === false) shows its owner a 'Hidden — only you can see this profile' badge on /u/:id.
userService.publicProfile derives verifications instead of returning []: phone (verified by OTP sign-in) and id (an approved KYC review on a service profile they own).

There is no separate activeRole state left: HatSwitcherCard derives the role from activeContext (activeRoleFromContext), and support/guide screens read the same derived value, so the two can't diverge.

BusinessAccessGuard renders PinEntrySheet instead of <Outlet /> whenever the business has a console password and this session hasn't unlocked it, so a deep link or a refresh lands on the password prompt, not the console. The unlock is per browser session (entityPasswordService.isSessionUnlocked).

useAccountOptions exposes `loading` (owned entities, businesses, provider profiles and access sessions all answered) and AccountSwitcher shows a skeleton until then, instead of a customer-only list with 'Add a business' that people mis-tapped.
ManageHub adds a 'Managed for others' section listing businesses with an ACTIVE access grant (businessAccessService.mySessions), so a delegated manager's /manage is no longer blank.
The RoleSwitcher dropdown is capped at min(70vh, 460px) with its own scroll (overscroll contained), so the actions below the account list stay reachable on a phone.
ProviderAccessGuard and BusinessAccessGuard reset the context with the user's own name instead of an empty string, so being turned away no longer blanks their name in headers.
The header pill has minHeight 44 in both themes (44px minimum touch target).

Confirmed as designed, with the limit written down: the console password is a device-level lock over the console UI (BusinessAccessGuard blocks the route until it's entered), not a server boundary — RLS authorises the owner's own session either way, so someone holding that session could still read the same rows through the API. Making it a real boundary needs server-issued, password-scoped grants; owner decision for v1.1. 20260983 hardens what exists: only the owner or a granted team member may attempt, per-attempter lockouts with backoff.

Migration 20260983: attempts are counted per (owner, kind, attempted_by), and verify_business_password/verify_provider_password refuse anyone who is neither the owner nor an active grantee without touching a counter. Forced-rollback tested on staging: before, five wrong guesses by a stranger or a team member locked the owner out (correct password → false); after, the owner still gets in, while their own five wrong guesses still lock them.

Removal already required the current password (PinEntrySheet mode='remove' → clear_entity_password verifies it). The missing half was any trace: migration 20260984 makes set_entity_password and clear_entity_password notify the owner ('Console password set/changed/removed', the removal noting the backup question went with it). Forced-rollback tested: before 'none', after all three notices.

Migration 20260983: each further lockout of the same person doubles (15 min, 30 min, … capped at 24 h) via entity_password_attempts.lockout_count, and a separate entity-wide brake (20 failures in the window across attempters) stops a crowd of accounts guessing in parallel while never blocking the owner. Verified on staging: first lockout 15 min, second 30 min; before the change both were 15.
